about: A full map (docs/adr/0108, D4): a put that names an outcome and finds the map full of other keys writes `full`, leaves the map as it was and raises nothing, so the document counts it; a put of a key the map holds replaces it however full the map is; the same put with no outcome raises error.execution and ends its block, as an append to a full list does. Expected values are derived from the document, not observed from a backend.

steps.note: the map holds its two: 3 is refused as a value, the map is as it was, and nothing is raised
2 is held: a full map replaces a key it holds
a put with no outcome into the full map fails: error.execution, and the block ends before `afterPut` counts it
with room for it, the same put goes last and the block runs on
